text:
The Kansas City Chiefs will find out how deep they are at running back this weekend.

That's because Kansas City ruled out star running back Kenneth Walker III for its Week 10 road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury he suffered in practice Friday. Kansas City elevated running back Nate Carter to the active roster.

Through Kansas City's first eight games, Walker has rushed for 872 yards – which is second in the NFL – and seven touchdowns on a career-high 5.5 yards per carry. Walker has also totaled 26 receptions – which is third on the Chiefs – for 172 yards and a team-high four touchdowns.

Kansas City's offense is second in the NFL in total yards (384.1 per game), tied for fourth in rushing yards (137.8 per game) and 10th outright in both passing yards (246.4 per game) and points (25.3 per game).

Elsewhere in the Chiefs' running back room, rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for 111 yards and one touchdown, with fellow rookie Jaydn Ott logging just three carries. Second-year back Brashard Smith is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. In all, Walker has accounted for 79.1% of Kansas City's total rushing yards (1,102).

Walker, who won Super Bowl LX MVP honors with the Seattle Seahawks last season, is in the first season of a three-year $43.1 million deal with the Chiefs.

Prior to defeating the New York Jets at home last week, the Chiefs lost back-to-back games on the road to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos. Kansas City is second in the AFC West at 6-2.

text:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

The NFL's second-leading rusher reported groin tightness on Friday morning and the team wants to "give him a week" to rest. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson will now handle first-team duties in Walker's absence.

Following Friday's practice, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters that the team wanted to see how Walker responded to treatment before making a final decision on his status for Week 10.

"We'll just see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab and through tomorrow," Reid said. "Somewhere he tweaked it. We're kind of feeling it out just to see where we're at with that [groin]. We're not going to put him at risk. If he can go, he can go. If he can't, he can't."

Walker was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report.

In his first season with the Chiefs after signing a three-year, $43.05 million contract in March, Walker has 872 rushing yards and seven touchdowns through eight games. He is currently eight yards behind the NFL leader Bijan Robinson of the Falcons.

Johnson, the team's fifth-round pick in the 2026 draft out of Nebraska, has 111 rushing yards and a touchdown, plus 14 receptions for 237 and a touchdown this season. He has also served as the Chiefs' kick return man, picking up 318 return yards on 11 attempts.

Walker has not only helped carry the Chiefs offense but has also been one of fantasy football's best players over the season's first half. He has averaged 22.9 fantasy points per game in half-PPR scoring, second only to Jahmyr Gibbs among all running backs.

With Walker out, Johnson is a must-add in all fantasy leagues. At the time the news broke of Walker being ruled out, the rookie was available in 56% of Yahoo leagues. That number will skyrocket. Johnson has been one of the most valuable fantasy stashes all season for just such a situation. He has shown flashes in limited touches this season, including posting 22.8 fantasy points in Week 8 thanks to five receptions for 128 yards and a touchdown. He also found the end zone last week in a win over the Jets. Johnson will be a borderline fantasy RB1 in a matchup at Atlanta.

The Falcons have been lit up by RBs recently with injuries taking a toll, allowing Bucky Irving (170 total yards), Christian McCaffrey (RB6) and D'Andre Swift (RB5) to run wild. They also just traded away safety Jessie Bates this week. This sets up a potential big game with the Chiefs projected for 25.25 points as 3.5-point road favorites.

text:
The San Francisco 49ers wrapped up their final practice of the week ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.

Coming off their Week 9 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, the 49ers saw positive developments at wide receiver, with Deebo Samuel Sr. returning to practice and newly acquired Keenan Allen completing his first week with the team.

Following Friday's practice, head coach Kyle Shanahan ruled out WR Mike Evans for Sunday's game and listed seven players as questionable, including T Trent Williams and LB Dre Greenlaw. Below is the full status report.

Questionable Players

Williams was added to the injury report after suffering a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice. The veteran tackle was limited Thursday before sitting out Friday.

"Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn't make you totally at ease," Shanahan said. "Sunday comes fast. But hopefully, that's enough time for him to be all right."

Greenlaw is also questionable after sustaining a knee injury on Thursday. The linebacker was limited on Thursday and Friday after a rest day on Wednesday. If unable to play, rookie LB Jaden Dugger could see an increased role after stepping up in Greenlaw's absence earlier this season.

"Hopefully we'll have Dre on Sunday," Shanahan said. "But if we don't, next man up, and our next man's proven himself so far."

CB Renardo Green (back) and DB Deommodore Lenoir (foot) both sustained injuries during the team's Week 9 win over the Raiders. Both missed Wednesday and Thursday practices before returning to limited participation on Friday. CB Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) was limited throughout the week. All three are questionable.

With those three defensive backs listed as questionable, CB Nate Hobbs could provide additional depth in the secondary if available. Hobbs is also questionable for Sunday, but practiced in full this week. The veteran remains on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated to the 53-man roster to play.

"Nate's a real good NFL corner," Shanahan said on Wednesday. "You could see him effective inside, effective outside, and his versatility is great, so wherever he's needed."

DL C.J. West (knee) returned to practice this week after the 49ers opened his 21-day practice window on Wednesday. West has been sidelined since Week 2 following knee surgery to remove a bone chip.

West was limited before returning to full participation on Friday. He remains questionable for Sunday, and if activated from IR it would mark his first game since Week 2. The lineman recorded a sack in the team's Week 1 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia.

Ruled-Out Players

Evans has been ruled out for Sunday's game as he continues recovering from his Achilles injury. Shanahan said Evans is making progress, but emphasized the importance of allowing him to fully recover.

"We're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again," Shanahan said. "But it's going in the right direction."

When asked about Evans' potential return, Shanahan said there is a chance he could be available next week.

Returning / No Game Designation

After missing the last three games with a hamstring injury sustained in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks, Deebo Samuel Sr. progressed from limited on Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday. The receiver carries no game designation.

"Had a good week, healthy," Shanahan said. "First week back, so he's still getting back into it."

Allen also completed his first three practices with the 49ers following his move from the Indianapolis Colts at the trade deadline. Shanahan confirmed that Allen will have a role against Dallas as he continues learning.

"He's catching up, putting a lot on his plate, working hard to get it, and expect him to get more and more each week," Shanahan said. "But it was a good first start this week."

RB Christian McCaffrey returned to full on Thursday and Friday after a Wednesday rest day. DB Siran Neal (knee, foot) was limited Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in full Friday. WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was a full participant throughout the week. All three carry no game designations.

Preparing for Dallas and Mexico

The 49ers embark on their two-week road trip starting with Dallas, then heading to Colorado Springs for altitude training before traveling to Mexico City for their second international game of the year.

The team will practice in Colorado Springs beginning Wednesday to help acclimate to the higher elevation ahead of its Week 11 matchup in Mexico City.

"I do think it makes you a couple percent better," Shanahan said of the altitude training. "Hopefully, we can take care of business this week, and then we'll get a couple days off for coaches to game plan. We'll start up in Colorado Wednesday, then we'll head to Mexico on Saturday. Looking forward to these two games."

text:
The Cleveland Browns might have seen the return of quarterback Deshaun Watson from concussion protocol after he missed last week's game.

But the team will now potentially be without a different key member of the offense this weekend.

On Friday, Nov. 13, the Browns announced another batch of injuries ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday.

First announced by ESPN NFL Insider Daniel Oyefusi, rookie wideout Denzel Boston was listed as questionable heading into the weekend due to a toe injury.

The 6-foot-4, 215-pound rookie has been one of the Browns' most exciting offseason additions to the offense, coming out of the draft quickly and making his impact. Across his first nine games, he has 32 receptions for 507 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 15.8 yards per reception.

His connection with Deshaun Watson has been one of the more welcomed things this season, even though the two had no prior experience with one another before this past offseason.

Without him on Sunday, Cleveland would have to turn to a combination of Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond to slide into the final wide receiver spot.

Alongside Boston potentially being inactive, the Browns received unfortunate news that safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton would be out on Sunday. Not listed as questionable, Burton is dealing with a calf injury, while Hickman is still recovering from a concussion.

Burton missing Sunday's game is going to be a hit to the rushing attack for the Browns, an area of the offense that has struggled all season long. With him out, the workload is going to be pushed even more onto the passing attack, especially with Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson still searching for a rhythm as the back half of the season gets underway.

While having any bodies on the injured list is going to be an issue, the Browns have found a nice replacement for Hickman for the time being.

Taken in the second round of the draft this past year, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren's initial status in the Browns' defense was somewhat unknown.

However, through limited opportunities, he has shown that he has an awful lot in the tank to give the team. Through nine games, he has 42 combined tackles, three tackles for a loss and three pass deflections, all while routinely being in the right position at the right time.

His role has changed each week, but in Week 10, it seems his opportunity to become a long-term, key piece of the Browns' defense is his for the taking.

The Browns and Texans will face at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field, with Boston's final status expected to be released prior to the game.

text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- The Tennessee Titans will be without multiple starters against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), left guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), punter Tommy Townsend (left knee), along with linebackers Cody Barton (concussion) and Anthony Hill Jr. (neck), were ruled out by coach Robert Saleh before practice Friday.

Tate is the reigning AFC Offensive Rookie of the Month after posting 21 receptions for 290 yards and a touchdown across four games in October. The shoulder injury occurred during Tennessee's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 and caused him to miss the following game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Tate's 413 receiving yards led all rookie pass catchers entering Week 9. The Titans were optimistic Tate would return after the bye week, but the shoulder "stuck on him a little bit," according to Saleh.

Second-year receiver Chimere Dike will get a chance to step up in Tate's absence. Dike logged a season-high 58 snaps with Tate out. He responded with five receptions for 61 yards and a touchdown.

"It's a new opportunity," Dike said. "Obviously, it's a naturally increased role with Tate being out. But my mindset's not that much different. Make the most of your opportunities and do whatever you can to help the team win."

Skoronski injured a hamstring in the fourth quarter against the Bengals before the bye week. He was carted from the sideline into the locker room and missed practice all week. Reserve offensive lineman James Hudson III played 30 snaps in Skoronski's place. Hudson is expected to get the start against Jacksonville, but Saleh said it will be a game-time decision.

Hill leads the Titans with 82 tackles and was named the AFC Defensive Rookie of the Month for September. This will be his first time missing a game after injuring his neck in Week 8. Barton suffered a concussion in the same game, opening the door for Cedric Gray to see an increased role. Gray was a starter during training camp but suffered a concussion in a UTV accident during Labor Day weekend that made him unavailable for the season opener and relegated him to a reserve role.

"It's something I've been looking forward to all year," Gray said Friday. "It's a long season, things happen, so I kind of knew that at some point my name would be called again. I'm just looking forward to the opportunity to get out there, play a full game on defense and show what I can do."

text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Independent medical experts will examine the circumstances around Jalen Hurts' blood clots and share their findings with the NFL and NFL Players Association as part of the forthcoming joint review, according to a league executive.

The NFL provided some additional details about the review as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware.

"As outlined by the league and NFLPA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties," executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement released by Blunt Rochester's office Friday.

"The League and Players Association also have several medical committees that review and monitor player injury data closely. For at least the past decade, the NFL has tracked clotting disorders among players every season through a subcommittee of its General Medical Committee, and this information is shared with the NFLPA. Following the ongoing joint review, the League and NFLPA will consider appropriate next steps, including whether this case points to a need for additional league-wide guidance."

The joint review into Hurts' situation has not officially begun as the NFL and NFLPA work to hammer out its parameters.

Hurts, 28, is expected to sit out the rest of the 2026 season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs in October.

He was originally diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London before the Philadelphia Eagles' Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. He played in the game, flew home with the team and practiced in full the following Wednesday before a follow-up ultrasound that evening showed the blood clot had moved.

Hurts was placed on injured reserve Oct. 17. Two days later, his agent, Nicole Lynn, and the team released a joint statement about Hurts, saying, "After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations."

His treatment involves anticoagulation or "blood thinners," which prevents him from participating in any contact activities, including football.

The NFLPA has not invoked Article 39 of the CBA, which allows the union to launch a formal investigation into the health, safety or medical care provided by club-affiliated personnel, but as the statement shows, some of its guidelines will be used during this process.

Under the CBA, the neutral physicians must issue a written report within 60 days of their selection, and their recommendations to address and correct any issues need to be acted upon by both parties.

Blunt Rochester penned a letter to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell in October seeking answers on the circumstances surrounding Hurts and clarity on the league's blood clot protocols.

In a statement Friday, Blunt Rochester expressed gratitude to the NFL for providing an update while encouraging the league to use its platform to further education around blood clots.

"We welcome the opportunity to provide additional information, and find ways to support your efforts around raising awareness and improving outcomes related to blood clot disorders," Miller wrote.

title: A.J. Brown may be back for the Patriots as pressure ramps up in season's second half
description:
In the bigger picture, the Patriots need a big second half from Brown, especially after a start to his tenure with the team that has been so sluggish.
Due to ankle and knee injuries, Brown has played in only three games this season and finished only one.
If Brown lives up to the Patriots' hopes in the second half of the season and in January, his slow start will be easily forgiven.
In the one full game he played this season, Brown caught only three passes on 10 targets and had several drops.
Still, teammates expressed optimism about what Brown's return to the practice field meant to them.
text:
MUNICH -- Here in the shadows of soccer power Bayern Munich's fancy digs, wide receiver A.J. Brown was joking around with New England Patriots teammates, a welcome return for a team that needs to get its quarterback more help.

Officially, it was just a return to the practice fields for now, as his status for Sunday's game remains questionable due to ankle and knee injuries. While Brown looks to be nearing a return, this weekend kicks off an important second half of the season -- whether he plays or not.

In the micro sense, Brown would be a welcome addition as the Patriots prepare for a struggling Detroit Lions secondary on Sunday. He could play a significant role in the passing game as New England looks to build momentum before its bye week.

In the bigger picture, the Patriots need a big second half from Brown, especially after a start to his tenure with the team that has been so sluggish.

Due to ankle and knee injuries, Brown has played in only three games this season and finished only one. He has struggled in all of them. He has just nine catches for 101 yards and is without a touchdown.

To say he's been underwhelming would be an understatement.

But the 5-4 Patriots are also in a decent place for a playoff spot given how the AFC has shaken out. They really need Brown to be at his best down the stretch and entering the postseason. If Brown lives up to the Patriots' hopes in the second half of the season and in January, his slow start will be easily forgiven.

While given his injuries, that may not be as simple as it sounds, Brown's comeback would at least start with a favorable matchup. The Lions defense ranks 26th in EPA per dropback and 24th in success rate. The unit lacks the kind of top-tier cornerback typically needed to slow a player like Brown. That should be encouraging for Brown and the Patriots.

He would also be the first in line of several important players returning from the injured list, one they hope will continue to get shorter as the playoffs near.

"I think the more that we can get everybody back, the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team," coach Mike Vrabel said before Friday's practice in Germany, a more upbeat session than a typical Friday after the team held a light walk-through Thursday night. "One guy certainly doesn't make the difference, but the more that we get guys back, that's exciting. The pieces can start to build and come together."

On the other hand, a fair amount of skepticism with Brown is certainly fair. Would the team be rushing him by trying to get him on the field Sunday?

In the one full game he played this season, Brown caught only three passes on 10 targets and had several drops. It was bad enough that the home fans mockingly cheered when he finally caught a pass. Add to those struggles the fact that Brown is coming off a knee injury, and some worry is warranted.

Of course, the knee injury opens the Patriots up to additional scrutiny. When Brown was on the trade block with the Philadelphia Eagles, some teams, including the Los Angeles Rams, expressed concern about Brown's recurring knee issues.

The Patriots, though, greenlit the trade, despite their knowledge of his past, in part because of Brown's relationship with Vrabel.

Still, teammates expressed optimism about what Brown's return to the practice field meant to them. (Brown did not speak to reporters on Friday.)

"It feels good just to have that leader back," fellow wideout DeMario Douglas said. "Just thank God every time he's on the field. You know, to see how successful he became. And, man, I just appreciate his improvement."

The importance of Brown to the Patriots was upped too when Romeo Doubs suffered a shoulder injury that landed him on injured reserve. Without the two of them, New England's wide receivers have struggled.

For as good as Douglas can be in his role, it's difficult to win when he's your No. 1 wide receiver. Same for Mack Hollins.

The Patriots made the massive offseason move to get Brown for a reason. They're expecting him to be their true No. 1. That will be underscored in the second half of this season. Remember, Brown has no more guaranteed money on his contract after 2027. So the Patriots need to get the most out of him this season and next. And so far, he's been a disappointment.

But if Brown can put these injuries and a slow start behind him, a strong second half would go a long way toward reshaping the narrative around his addition and would be a massive boost to a Patriots offense in need of a top-tier receiver.

text:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock had a good week of practice as he prepares to fill in again for Sam Darnold on Sunday against the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders (4:05 p.m. ET, CBS) -- this time despite a pair of ailments of his own.

Lock was already dealing with an injury to his right elbow when he hurt his oblique last Sunday in Seattle's 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. He was again limited in practice all week, as has been the case since the start of Week 6.

"Similar cadence in workload in terms of last week," Macdonald said Friday. "It's good to have done it and gotten through the week well. I know he's confident and optimistic, so we're in good shape."

In addition to Darnold (quad, rib) and left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) -- whom Macdonald had ruled out earlier in the week -- the Seahawks will be without defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) and left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) again Sunday.

They'll get outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and wide receiver/kick returner Rashid Shaheed (knee) back against the Raiders after each missed the past two games. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed will play Sunday after missing two days this week to tend to a personal matter.

Lock said Thursday that he was feeling good, and that his oblique injury wasn't impacting his throwing all that much. It's on his right side, which Lock said is "way better" for a right-handed quarterback than a left oblique injury, which caused him to miss two weeks during the preseason when he was with the New York Giants in 2024.

"I feel like we did a great job handling the week last week, and here we are, we've just got a little something added to it, and I think we're doing the same," Lock said. "We're doing a great job getting ready."

Macdonald said that No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe "has done a tremendous job" while taking reps with the Seahawks' No. 1 offense as the team continues to manage Lock's workload in practice.

Sunday's game will mark Lock's third start this season and the fourth time he has stepped in for Darnold, who hurt his glute on the fifth play of the opener, then suffered a cracked rib and a quad injury in Week 8.

Macdonald has said Darnold might return for the Seahawks' game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, following Seattle's bye.

"I see Sam progressing with his rehab," Macdonald said. "The guys are saying he's doing a great job, and he's progressing. We'll take it a day and a week at a time."

Williams will miss his second straight game because of a stinger. He took part in pre-practice warmups Wednesday and Thursday but was listed as a nonparticipant all week.

"It's more of a contact thing," Macdonald said. "So, he's done a good job of staying in shape and staying fresh. He's in the meetings. He's doing all the Leo things. He's just not playing right now."

text:
Fans have been itching to see more of former Toledo standout Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, and they’re about to get their wish in Week 10.

The Cleveland Browns ruled out starting safety Ronnie Hickman Friday as he continues to work through the NFL’s concussion protocol. That means McNeil-Warren will step into a full-time role on defense alongside veteran Grant Delpit against the Houston Texans on Sunday.

Head coach Todd Monken called it a great opportunity for McNeil-Warren, who’s gotten some run on defense throughout the season in Cleveland’s three safety packages.

“That’s never easy when you’ve got two established safeties in front of you,” Monken said. “You know, pretty much right from the get-go. The young receivers were thrown in, right? Where E-man, it’s been a little bit slower process and getting the amount of snaps that you need. But talk about range, talk about physicality, and he’s really got a high football IQ that I didn’t — It’s not that I didn’t think he had one way or the other. I didn’t know that when we took him. So, I think he’s got a really bright future.”

Here’s a full breakdown of the Browns’ Week 10 injury report, including one injury that fans will want to monitor throughout the weekend.

Browns final injury report before Week 10 showdown against Texans

Ronnie Hickman, S (concussion)

Game status: Out

Monken told reporters that Hickman entered the NFL’s return-to-play protocol after last week’s loss to the Saints, but he was unable to practice Wednesday through Friday.

With extended rest coming during Cleveland’s Week 11 bye, Hickman should have a good shot at returning Nov. 29 against the Raiders.

Denzel Boston, WR (toe)

Game status: Questionable

Both Monken and Boston himself have expressed optimism about his chances of playing against the Texans, but his lack of practice activity this week is at least moderately concerning.

Boston was expected to practice on Thursday but wound up sitting. He was a limited participant on Friday.

“He came out there today and moved around. Moved around pretty good,” Monken said. “Went through our walk, took a full walk. But then when we got out there, we just limited his reps. So, we’ll have to see how he progresses tomorrow and then Sunday. But it’s trending in the right way.”

Michael Burton, FB (calf)

Game status: Out

No surprises here. The 34-year-old Burton injured his calf during last week’s game against the Saints, and with the bye week looming, there was no reason to rush him back at less than 100 percent. The veteran hasn’t been a major part of the offense, and the run game has struggled whether or not he’s been on the field.

The quarterback has a fracture and dislocation of his right thumb, his throwing hand, following the injury he sustained in Week 8.

His head coach stated that his recovery is progressing well, but has set no return date.

Lamar Jackson: no return date set

In his official statement, Jesse Minter stressed the variable nature of recovery timelines.

The six-to-ten-week window is therefore neither a definitive medical milestone nor an announcement that his season is over.

For a quarterback, healing alone is not enough: he must also regain the strength and precision needed to grip and throw the ball. This is explained in part by a hand surgery specialist interviewed by UofL Health, though their analysis does not constitute a personal diagnosis of Jackson.

Just one play against the Bills

Getty Images

Lamar Jackson was injured on 1 November, on Baltimore's very first offensive play against the Buffalo Bills. His right hand struck defender Gregory Rousseau as he attempted a pass.

The two-time MVP had only just returned after missing three games with an ankle injury. His backup, Tyler Huntley, also left the game with a toe injury, forcing rookie Joe Fagnano to step in.

The Ravens placed Jackson and Huntley on injured reserve on 5 November.

Jacoby Brissett steps in

Getty Images

To stabilise their Offense, the Ravens signed Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. The veteran is expected to start against the Los Angeles Chargers on the upcoming Monday Night Football.

Baltimore go into that game with a record of four wins and five losses and have lost four games in a row. Brissett is set to become the franchise's fourth starting quarterback this season, after Jackson, Huntley and Fagnano.

The Ravens must move forward without Jackson

The challenge is no longer simply a matter of waiting for their quarterback. To keep their ambitions alive, the Ravens must build an Offense capable of functioning without his improvisation, his rushing ability and the space it creates.

Derrick Henry can provide a foundation in the running game, but Baltimore must also protect Brissett and find greater consistency in the passing game. Signing a veteran does not automatically resolve collective struggles.

A potential return from Lamar Jackson will only have a meaningful impact if the Ravens remain in contention. Their challenge is therefore twofold: allow their quarterback to recover and win enough games in his absence.

After experiencing back spasms in pregame warmups last week against the Texans, the Chargers wide receiver was unable to take the field. With his Week 10 status up in the air, here is a look at the latest updates on his health.

Ladd McConkey Suffers Pregame Back Injury

During pregame warmups last Sunday, McConkey experienced back spasms. Despite being previously listed as active, he was unable to take the field in any fashion.

After the game began, the Chargers announced he was questionable to return due to a back injury. It was a bit of an odd case, with the team announcing the injury after the game began, even though the Chargers wide receiver never took a snap during the 44-22 loss to Houston.

Because McConkey sustained the injury after the Chargers had already announced their inactive list, the wideout ended up being active but unavailable for the second time in three games.

Injuries have made it hard for McConkey to strengthen his rapport with Justin Herbert this season. This issue may spill over into Week 10 as the wideouts availability is murky at best.

For an offense that has struggled to establish any consistency, McConkey's potential absence would be another significant setback. The Chargers desperately need their offensive weapons healthy, but until McConkey returns to practice, his availability against Baltimore remains a question mark.

text:
Two days before the Kansas City Chiefs kick off their road tilt with the Falcons, they received some extremely concerning news on the injury front this afternoon.

During Andy Reid's media availability, he revealed that star running back Kenneth Walker III is dealing with a groin injury. As a result, Walker did not participate in Friday's practice session and could be designated as questionable leading up to the matchup.

"Kenneth Walker came in this morning and had a tight groin, so we just sat him out of practice," Reid told reporters today. "We'll see how he feels this afternoon with rehab and through tomorrow."

Reid explained that Walker informed the coaching staff in the morning that he had tweaked something and needed to get checked out. He also noted that Walker isn't the kind of player to sit out unless something is really bothering him.

The former Seahawks tailback has been sensational in his first year in Kansas City, leading the NFL in rushing yards per game and amassing over 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 11 total touchdowns across eight appearances. However, there appears to be a chance he is absent from the lineup this Sunday.

Walker was always considered an injury-prone player in Seattle, though his only scare with the Chiefs before this one was a minor ankle ailment that forced him to miss the preseason finale. The 2025 campaign marked the first time in his career that he was able to suit up for all 17 games.

What Kenneth Walker's Absence Would Mean for Kansas City

If the highly anticipated ground game battle between Walker and Bijan Robinson doesn't take place, fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson will make his first NFL start in the backfield. Reid said that he would be the next Chief in line for carries and expressed confidence in his ability.

The Nebraska product has been remarkably productive lately, as he's totaled 177 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on just 12 touches over the past two weeks. He is a dynamic rusher who ranks among the NFL's best at forcing missed tackles, even with limited opportunities.

Aside from Johnson, Kansas City's running back depth is dangerously thin. Brashard Smith is currently on injured reserve, while third-string Jadyn Ott is questionable for Sunday's contest with a hamstring injury. Should he and Walker not be available this weekend, the Chiefs will only have one active ball carrier on the roster before making any corresponding moves.

Because of how late Walker popped up on the injury radar, it's difficult to say what his outlook is for KC's Week 10 matchup, but initial indications certainly aren't too promising. Reid did not disclose whether Walker's groin started tightening up recently or whether he had been battling through it for some time.

Fans should soon find out more about the severity of this injury and whether he can take the field at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

text:
Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett expects to play Sunday despite missing practice, while cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable for their game at the Arizona Cardinals.

Garrett was held out of practice on Friday after being limited earlier in the week because of a knee injury that caused him to miss seven games before returning to make three sacks with a forced fumble in the Rams’ 20-13 win at the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

"He’s had a really good week," coach Sean McVay said. "Played a bunch of snaps, and expect him to be able to build on that. But we’re being smart with him."

Garrett was largely pleased with his performance, in which he played 61.5% of the defensive snaps, apart from needing to build up his endurance and address what he felt was a slow get-off time.

"I'm sure Next Gen or PFF or somebody would tell me it wasn't too bad," Garrett said. "It felt terrible to me."

McDuffie is dealing with a back injury that forced him to miss the Rams’ third straight win last week, getting them over .500 for the first time this season at 5-4. McVay expressed optimism he would be able to play, provided McDuffie felt good coming out of Friday's workout.

"He was rolling, you know, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday," McVay said.

The ongoing issues with the Rams’ two marquee offseason acquisitions are indicative of their larger injury crisis that has threatened a campaign that began with them as Super Bowl betting favorites. Los Angeles is so beat up that star wide receiver Puka Nacua was placed on injured reserve Thursday to free up a roster spot, a reversal from what McVay had indicated earlier in the week when he cited the limited number of IR slots remaining to be able to bring players back later in the season.

"Some things changed where we needed that spot because of all the moving pieces," said McVay, while adding that nothing has changed with the timeline for Nacua’s return from knee and toe injuries.

Safety Kam Curl is questionable with a toe injury, but McVay indicated he is likely to play. The same is expected for the Rams’ banged-up crop of tight ends, Colby Parkinson (ribs), Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique). All three are needed to supplement the passing game with top receivers Nacua, Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) on IR.

Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) and left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) were ruled officially out, as was previously announced.

The Rams were upset by the Cardinals 18-16 on Oct. 18, giving up a last-minute drive which ended with Chad Ryland kicking his sixth field goal as time expired at SoFi Stadium.

text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers listed 12 players as out, doubtful or questionable, including seven starters, for Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings.

Four players are out: running back Josh Jacobs (finger), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Jacobs, Rhyan and Whyle didn’t practice this week; Parsons practiced all week but the team wants to give him one more week to get ready.

“He looks great but he just doesn’t have a ton of reps under his belt,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “So, we want to try to continue to build him up.”

Linebacker LB Zaire Franklin (shin), who didn’t practice all week, is doubtful and almost certainly will miss a fourth consecutive game.

Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Franklin are starters. Four more starters are questionable: safety Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), safety Xavier McKinney (foot) and edge Lukas Van Ness (back).

McKinney (foot) was added to the injury report on Friday. Right guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle and triceps) practiced on Wednesday and Thursday but did not practice on Friday. Zeitler’s status could impact the team’s plan at guard; left guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) is off the injury report.

McKinney is tied for the NFL lead with five interceptions.

Good News for Two Starters

Van Ness and Bullard returned to practice after missing the first two days of the week. Bullard said he’d play after Thursday’s practice and Van Ness essentially said the same thing on Friday.

“I’m doing good, thank you,” Van Ness said. “It felt good to get back on the grass today.”

Van Ness leads the team with 4.5 sacks. Of the 70 edge defenders with at least 140 pass-rushing snaps, Van Ness ranks 13th in pass-rush win rate, according to Pro Football Focus.

“It’s a weekly challenge, always finding something to improve on,” Van Ness said. “Coach LaFleur always says it’s 1 percent. You’re either getting worse or you’re getting better. No matter who you’re talking about, anyone can find something to improve on.

“We’ve come back week after week, evaluated the tape and continue to keep our nose down and our head down and keep working. If we see that, you talk about December and January football, that’s when you see these teams really come together and then compete for a Super Bowl.”

Running back Chris Brooks (ankle) and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle), who have been designated to return, were limited participation all week and are questionable. To play on Sunday, they will have to be added to the roster on Saturday.

Big Vikings News

After Friday’s practice, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters that Kirk Cousins will start at quarterback.

“The way he threw the football this week, it’s a really cool thing to see,” O’Connell said.

However, tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) are out. Another starter, defensive end Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), is out, as well.

Cashman is a stud. With 76 tackles, he is one of 18 players with 70-plus tackles this season. He leads that group with 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for losses and 10 quarterback hits and is tied with Packers safety Evan Williams for first with seven passes defensed.

Hockenson leads the team with 35 catches; the next Vikings tight end, Gavin Bartholomew, has only seven.

Receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was added to the injury report and is questionable. He was limited participation at Friday’s practice.

Saluting Lukas Van Ness

For the second consecutive year, Lukas Van Ness is Green Bay’s nominee for the NFL’s Salute to Service Award. In its 16th year, the award honors a league member who demonstrates “an exceptional commitment” to honoring and supporting the military.

Van Ness’ grandfather served 27 years and earned the rank of lieutenant colonel in the U.S. Army.

“It’s really an honor to be able to recognize all the amazing men and women that support our country and allow us to do what we do out here on the football field,” he said. “Being able to do this for my second year is really special, especially with my grandfather, who served.”

He added: “We have a platform of being able to bring recognition to those service members and those who have served and then, ultimately, those who have paid the ultimate sacrifice for not only us but our country, it’s really, really special. It’s a really cool initiative that the NFL does.”

The Packers have won five of their last six games, due in large part to the play of the defense, which has done more than survive without Micah Parsons.

“We just have a really competitive group of guys,” he said of the edge group of Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox and Dani Dennis-Sutton. “Whether it’s myself or Barryn or B-Cox or Dani, there’s no fall-off in talent.

“We’re all super-capable. We can all go out there and play at a high level. It’s been really fun to be able to rotate out there with different guys, work on some different packages and have the flexibility to throw us wherever on the field on any given circumstance. I’m really proud of how we’re all playing. It’s been cool to see us all step up.”

Packers Final Injury Report

Out: RB Josh Jacobs (finger), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), C Sean Rhyan (ankle), TE Josh Whyle (concussion).

Doubtful: LB Zaire Franklin (shin).

Questionable: RB Chris Brooks (ankle), S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), G/T Travis Glover (knee), S Xavier McKinney (foot), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps).

No injury designation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip), LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness), WR Bo Melton (gameday concussion evaluation), K Trey Smack (right calf), WR Savion Williams (groin),

Note: Brooks, Moore and Parsons have been designated to return and are within their 21-day practice window.

Vikings Final Injury Report

Out: LB Blake Cashman (concussion), TE T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest), DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), WR Jauan Jennings (calf), QB Kyler Murray (hamstring).

Doubtful: None.

Questionable: WR Jordan Addison (thumb), S Josh Metellus (shoulder), OLB Kyle Van Noy (calf).

No injury designation: S Theo Jackson (quad), S Jay Ward (knee), QB Carson Wentz (ankle).

text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers had two important additions to their injury report this week with left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (knee) now listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.

According to coach Kyle Shanahan, Williams and Greenlaw suffered their injuries in Thursday's practice, with both players listed as limited for that day because of it. Greenlaw was again limited Friday, while Williams did not practice.

"Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn't make you totally at ease," Shanahan said of Williams. "Sunday comes fast, but hopefully that's enough time for him to be all right."

If Williams is unable to play, the Niners will turn to swing tackle Vederian Lowe to step into the lineup. And if Greenlaw can't play, rookie Jaden Dugger will move into the weakside linebacker spot, according to Shanahan.

"Hopefully we'll have Dre on Sunday, but if we don't, next man up, and our next man's proven himself so far," Shanahan said.

Elsewhere on the injury report, wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) will miss his third straight game. He's the only Niner officially ruled out against the Cowboys as he continues to work his way through the tendinitis that flared up in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders.

Shanahan offered a bit more clarity Friday afternoon on when Evans could return, saying there's "a chance" for next week against the Minnesota Vikings but adding that he's "not sure yet."

"It's been going well," Shanahan said. "I'm sure if this was the last game or something, he'd be able to go out there. But we're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again, but it's going in the right direction."

In addition to Williams and Greenlaw, all three of San Francisco's top cornerbacks -- Deommodore Lenoir (foot), Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) -- are questionable against the Cowboys.

So, too, are defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) and defensive back Nate Hobbs (adductor), both of whom are working their way back from injured reserve and could be activated Saturday.

Meanwhile, wide receiver Deebo Samuel, who has been out with a hamstring injury since Week 5, practiced all week and is cleared to return against the Cowboys.

"He had a good week, healthy," Shanahan said. "First week back, so he's still getting back into it, but [he] took care of himself real well while he was injured and had a good week."

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- The Chiefs listed running back Kenneth Walker III as questionable for Sunday's road game against the Atlanta Falcons after he missed Friday's practice with a groin injury.

Coach Andy Reid said Walker reported tightness in his groin to the team in the morning before the Chiefs' final on-field practice of the week, resulting in the running back being held out of the session as a precautionary measure.

"We'll just see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab and through tomorrow," Reid said. "Somewhere he tweaked it. We're kind of feeling it out just to see where we're at with that [groin]. We're not going to put him at risk. If he can go, he can go. If he can't, he can't."

Walker, who joined the Chiefs in March after signing a three-year, $43.05 million contract, has been one of the NFL's best offseason acquisitions. He enters Week 10 with 872 rushing yards, second in the league behind Atlanta's Bijan Robinson (880).

If Walker is unable to play, the Chiefs are expected to rely heavily on rookie running back Emmett Johnson, the fifth-round pick who has played most often on third downs. In eight games, Johnson has been effective as a runner (111 rushing yards and one touchdown on 26 attempts) and a receiver (237 yards and one touchdown on 14 receptions).

"He'll be ready to go," right guard Trey Smith said Friday regarding Johnson, who could make his first career start. "I like Emmett, man, his juice, his energy. He oozes enthusiasm, emotion and positive energy. You can tell the guy wants to be great, and you can tell he works at it. He really cares, man. I'm really excited for him. It's not hard to root for guys like that."

Meanwhile, the Chiefs expect to have wide receiver Xavier Worthy available after he left in the second half of last week's win over the Jets with a hamstring injury. That should take a little pressure off Josh Downs, who intends to play after being acquired from the Colts just before the NFL trade deadline Tuesday in an attempt to build out Kansas City's depth at the position.

"I thought he did a nice job for what we asked him to do, to digest everything in a couple days," Reid said of Downs. "He's a smart kid and knows how to play. He's been playing, which is great, and playing at a high level. He worked into the things we asked him to do and did well. I think he's ready to play in a game for us."

Downs had 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown in nine games with Indianapolis.

The Chiefs expect to have first-round pick Mansoor Delane back after the cornerback missed a couple of games with a shoulder injury. However, they likely will be without right tackle Jaylon Moore because of an ankle injury and Peter Woods due to a neck injury.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

title: NFL-Ravens quarterback Jackson out 6-10 weeks with thumb injury - Dewitt Daily News
description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) – Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between 6 to 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb, head coach Jesse Minter said on Friday.
Jackson, a two-time NFL Most Valuable Player, suffered the injury on the Ravens’ first offensive play in a November 1 game against the Buffalo Bills.
He could still return this season if the struggling Ravens can get back into the postseason picture.
His return was short-lived as he appeared to strike his throwing hand against the helmet of a Bills player before immediately leaving the field.
The Ravens, who have lost four consecutive games and are last in the AFC North division with a 4-5 record, host the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday.
text:
Nov 13 (Reuters) – Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between 6 to 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb, head coach Jesse Minter said on Friday.

Jackson, a two-time NFL Most Valuable Player, suffered the injury on the Ravens’ first offensive play in a November 1 game against the Buffalo Bills. He could still return this season if the struggling Ravens can get back into the postseason picture.

“Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal,” Minter said in a statement. “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.”

Jackson made a strong start to the 2026 NFL season before missing three games with an ankle sprain suffered in a Week 4 clash against the Tennessee Titans.

His return was short-lived as he appeared to strike his throwing hand against the helmet of a Bills player before immediately leaving the field.

The Ravens, who have lost four consecutive games and are last in the AFC North division with a 4-5 record, host the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday.

text:
Heading into Week 10, New England ruled out starting CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee), and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). The Patriots are also listing nine players as questionable for Sunday's game vs. the Lions: WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), S Kevin Byard III (chest), TE Cameron Latu (back), OL Walter Rouse (concussion), S Brenden Schooler (hamstring), CB Charles Woods (hamstring), FB Reggie Gilliam (knee), and C/G Greg Van Roten (hamstring).

On offense, star wideout A.J. Brown returned to practice this week after sitting out the last two games with a knee injury that flared up in practice. Brown practiced in a limited capacity throughout the week and seems to be tracking toward returning as soon as Sunday. The Pats top wideout has played in only 3-of-9 games this season, catching nine passes for 101 receiving yards. Obviously, that's not the result anyone hoped for when the Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown this offseason.

That said, there's still plenty of season left for Brown to make an impact. The 29-year-old's return to practice is a positive sign. However, there's also a discussion to be had about Brown returning when the Patriots bye week follows their game in Munich. New England might hold off on Brown's return until after their Week 11 bye, giving him an extra two weeks of rest. Based on his practice participation and the fact that he made the trip, all signs point toward Brown playing on Sunday.

At running back, the Patriots could be down their top two backs on Sunday. Along with Henderson being out due to illness, top RB Rhamondre Stevenson is officially questionable after participating in a limited capacity in the two practices in Munich. Early reports indicated that Stevenson would miss games due to his knee injury, so it's a pleasant surprise that the Pats lead back at least has a chance to play on Sunday.

If Stevenson can't play or is limited, third back Corey Kiner figures to get a bulk of the early-down carries. Kiner has shown good burst, vision, and jump-cut ability in limited carries. He's averaging an impressive 4.9 yards per rush and has seven explosive runs (10-plus yards). Kiner has been a nice find and was pushing for more carries even in a healthy backfield. However, Stevenson is also a highly productive back in the passing game, both as a receiver and pass blocker.

The Pats RB1 hauled in a 30-yard touchdown vs. Green Bay last week, creating a mismatch against a linebacker on a wheel route, while Stevenson has almost weekly blocking highlights in blitz protection. To manage Stevenson's knee injury, one option might be to have him play only in passing situations. Along with his ability to execute blocks, the Patriots blitz-protection system is highly complex, so Stevenson at less than 100 percent might be New England's best option, even if it's just in a limited role on passing downs.

New England tried second-year RB Lan Larison in passing situations when Stevenson left the loss to the Packers, and Larison struggled in pass protection (two pressures). If Stevenson is inactive, the Patriots could also elevate practice-squad RB Terrell Jennings. However, Jennings is more of a downhill between-the-tackles runner. So, whether New England's healthy backs can execute in blitz protection is a huge question mark.

Along with the running backs blocking, the Patriots are also tracking toward starting their sixth different offensive line combination through 10 games. Backup G Walter Rouse is working through the NFL's concussion protocol. Rouse still has a chance to play, while the Pats could activate veteran C/G Greg Van Roten from injured reserve, who was a full participant in Friday's practice. New England's most likely starting five is LT Will Campbell, LG Greg Van Roten, C Jared Wilson, RG Matt Pryor, and RT Morgan Moses.

Moving over to the defense, the Patriots are once again shorthanded at cornerback with Davis III (knee) set to miss his fifth game this season. Davis will miss his fifth game of the season due to his injured knee, after missing four games with a neck injury. After being a late scratch last week, the good news is that fourth CB Charles Woods (hamstring) practiced all three days and was a full participant Friday.

Hopefully, Woods's increased workload in practice is a sign he's on track to play vs. the Lions. Woods has mostly been the Patriots top backup at outside corner when Davis or Christian Gonzalez are out. On Sunday, one would think that the Patriots would lean on Gonzalez, Woods, and NCB Marcus Jones, while rookie CB Karon Prunty serves as the fourth cornerback. The Pats could also elevate CB Kindle Vildor from the practice squad as more experienced depth behind its three starting corners.

With the team continuing to manage injuries, the Patriots could activate Gilliam and Van Roten from injured reserve on Saturday. New England has now used five of its eight IR-return designations on WR Mack Hollins, OT Marcus Bryant, Brown, Gilliam, and Van Roten. The Patriots only have three more IR-return spots for the rest of the regular season, with WR Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) as top return candidates after the Patriots Week 11 bye.

After ruling out three players, the Patriots will likely use practice squad elevations to add roster depth. Depending on Stevenson's status, Jennings could be elevated from the practice squad, as could backup guards Andrew Rupcich or Xavier Newman-Johnson. If the Pats don't need guard or running back depth, Vildor could be an option as well – we'll keep you updated.

The Patriots will then square off against the Lions at Allianz Stadium in Munich on Sunday.

title: NFL midseason superlatives and lessons: Josh Allen for MVP, all-in moves, dashed hopes
description:
With nine weeks of action in the books, the NFL regular season has reached its midway point.
Cousins, now 38 but among the league leaders in passing yards and touchdowns this season, should elevate a Vikings offense with plenty of talented receivers.
The San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs upgraded their wide receiver units by adding Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, respectively.
Scoring holds steady Teams have combined to score 45.93 points per game this season, according to NFL Research.
Superlative check-in MVP — QB Josh Allen, Buffalo Bills It’s a crowded race for the NFL’s highest individual honor.
text:
With nine weeks of action in the books, the NFL regular season has reached its midway point. We’ve learned quite a bit about this year’s teams, players and coaches, and how every piece fits into the puzzle and the ways in which the campaign has taken shape.

A lot can (and will) change between now and the end of Week 18, but by now we have a good idea of who leads the pack, who has some catching up to do and who is all but hopeless.

The NFL never disappoints, and the season’s homestretch will deliver all manner of compelling developments.

Here are some lessons and superlatives so far.

Lessons learned

Nothing is promised

The Los Angeles Rams looked like the team to beat when training camps opened in late July. Hardly anything has gone their way since.

Their trouble started with a disastrous travel plan for the opener in Australia, followed by prized offseason acquisition Myles Garrett’s Week 1 knee injury and surgery, repeated special teams woes and injuries to top wideouts Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Garrett returned in Week 9 and played like his usual game-wrecking self, but Sean McVay and his 5-4 Rams have a long road to realize their Super Bowl aspirations. Los Angeles has a 41 percent chance of making the postseason, according to The Athletic’s playoff simulator.

The Rams aren’t the only projected contender whose plans have gone awry. The Baltimore Ravens lost their top two quarterbacks — Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley — in just over a quarter of their Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills. That led the Ravens to start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, himself on a hobbled ankle, against the mighty Jacksonville Jaguars four days later. A disastrous performance pushed Baltimore (4-5) to trade for veteran Jacoby Brissett, with the hope that he can string together some wins in case Jackson returns from thumb surgery for a late playoff push.

Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles envisioned a bounce-back season after last year’s wild-card round exit. But injuries — including Jalen Hurts’ mind-bending blood clot situation — derailed those plans. General manager Howie Roseman has since unloaded veterans for draft picks to facilitate an offseason rebuild.

Drastic times call for drastic measures

The Minnesota Vikings opened the season with a league-best 6-0 record thanks in large part to a dominant defense helmed by coordinator Brian Flores. But the team’s hope that offseason pickup Kyler Murray would settle into coach Kevin O’Connell’s system and direct a good-enough offense never materialized. Then Murray suffered a hamstring injury during the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions, and backup Carson Wentz filled in for the next outing with a dismal showing on “Monday Night Football.”

In danger of wasting a championship-caliber defense, the Vikings traded a third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for quarterback Kirk Cousins, who played in Minnesota from 2018 to 2023. Cousins, now 38 but among the league leaders in passing yards and touchdowns this season, should elevate a Vikings offense with plenty of talented receivers. If he and O’Connell can produce a top-10 attack, Minnesota has a legitimate shot at contending for its first Super Bowl.

When within striking distance …

With both conferences wide open, front-runners made aggressive moves before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Most teams, like the Vikings, attempted to improve weak spots on their rosters.

The Jaguars swung big, acquiring defensive playmakers Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III. The San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs upgraded their wide receiver units by adding Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, respectively. The 49ers also brought back Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, while the Seattle Seahawks bolstered their offensive line with guard Quenton Nelson and the Bills addressed their secondary with safety Amani Hooker.

These contenders will continue fine-tuning their lineups in hopes of peaking during the playoffs.

Defense matters

Everyone loves offensive fireworks, but we’ve once again been reminded that it’s hard to win consistently without a quality defense. The Dallas Cowboys have one of the NFL’s best offenses, but their inability to stop opposing teams has left them with a 4-5 record and a 32 percent chance of making the playoffs, according to The Athletic’s projections. The 4-5 Raiders (7 percent chance to make the postseason) have a similar profile.

In fact, all 15 of the NFL’s worst scoring defenses have losing records.

Scoring holds steady

Teams have combined to score 45.93 points per game this season, according to NFL Research. That’s down slightly from 46.74 points per game halfway through last season, and a tick higher than the 45.36 points per game after nine weeks in 2024.

Down to the wire

The league has seen plenty of close finishes this season. Through nine weeks, 77 games have come down to one score (eight or fewer points). That ties the 2016 season for the third-most through Week 9 in NFL history, trailing only the 2024 (79) and 2022 (79) seasons.

Of those 77 games, 41 have featured a game-winning score in the final five minutes of regulation or overtime. That’s the second-most through Week 9, trailing only the 2021 season, which featured 42 such finishes. In 25 games, the winning team rallied from at least 10 points down, which ties the 2011 season for the fourth-most in league history. That figure trails the 1987 (30), 2020 (26) and 2022 (26) seasons.

Special teams spike

The NFL implemented its “dynamic kickoff” before the 2024 season to help the play regain relevance after years of teams booming the ball out of the end zone and settling for touchbacks rather than risking big returns.

The changes have seemingly done the trick, as the number of kickoff returns (1,118) and kickoff return yards (28,896) mark the most in league history through nine weeks.

Superlative check-in

MVP — QB Josh Allen, Buffalo Bills

It’s a crowded race for the NFL’s highest individual honor. Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has bounced back from last year’s injury-plagued campaign, leading the league with 298.3 passing yards per game and 23 passing touchdowns against six interceptions. He also ranks first in passer rating (114.8) and completion percentage (74.0) among quarterbacks who’ve thrown at least 100 passes.

Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love is also playing the best ball of his career, averaging 290.9 passing yards per game (second) with 19 touchdown passes (third), a 97.9 passer rating and six interceptions. And how about 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy? The 2022 Mr. Irrelevant has been anything but, with 247.5 passing yards per game, 17 touchdown passes, a 109.8 passer rating, a 69.1 percent completion rate and five interceptions for the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers.

All of those signal callers deserve recognition, but Allen carries the Bills and impacts opposing defenses in ways no other quarterback can. Averaging 253.4 passing yards with 12 touchdown passes, six interceptions and nine rushing touchdowns, Allen has led Buffalo to a 7-1 start while pacing an offense that averages a league-high 32.0 points a game and masking the struggles of a defense that yields 330.4 yards and 23.4 points per contest.

Offensive player of the year — QB Joe Burrow, Cincinnati Bengals

Burrow appears on pace to win the passing title, and despite competition from running backs Jahmyr Gibbs (847 rushing yards, nine touchdowns) and Bijan Robinson (880 rushing yards, five touchdowns), Burrow feels like the most deserving choice.

Defensive player of the year — Edge Will Anderson Jr., Houston Texans

The fourth-year pro leads the league with 9.5 sacks and is on pace to shatter his career-best mark of 12. Also making strong cases for themselves: linebacker Fred Warner (77 tackles, five forced fumbles) and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (48 tackles, six sacks, six pass breakups and 11 quarterback hits).

Offensive rookie of the year — WR Denzel Boston, Cleveland Browns

We’ll see what kind of numbers and impact quarterback Fernando Mendoza delivers over the final eight games, but Boston gets the nod for now, thanks to his 32 catches, 507 yards and three touchdowns.

Defensive rookie of the year – LB Arvell Reese, New York Giants

The No. 5 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has racked up 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss, 49 solo tackles (68 total), a forced fumble and an interception for the surprising Giants.

Coach of the Year — John Harbaugh, New York Giants

Ben Johnson continues to lead an impressive Chicago Bears team, and Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers rank among the Super Bowl favorites.

But with the Giants unexpectedly leading their division and contending for their first playoff berth since the 2022 season — with a backup quarterback, no less — Harbaugh gets the nod.

Comeback Player of the Year — Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs

The two-time league MVP and three-time Super Bowl champion adds more hardware to his collection. He’s made a seamless return from a torn ACL and LCL to lead the Chiefs back to contention.

text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens say Lamar Jackson's dislocated and broken right thumb has a typical recovery timeline of six to 10 weeks, with a source telling ESPN the quarterback has undergone surgery for the injury.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter addressed Jackson's status in a statement released by the team Friday in which he said recovery timelines are "challenging to predict."

"He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."

With nine weeks remaining in the regular season, Jackson could come back as early as Week 16 against the Cleveland Browns. If Jackson needs 10 weeks to recover, a return would come in the postseason.

The Ravens (4-5) have lost four straight games but are one game out of the final playoff spot in the AFC. Baltimore's playoff chances are projected at 3.7%, according to ESPN Analytics.

To help keep the team's postseason hopes alive, the Ravens traded for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is set to start Monday night in Baltimore against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.

Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first play of a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. His right hand hit the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau while trying to throw a pass.

This is the second significant injury this season for Jackson, who missed three games with a high ankle sprain. He has played only 14 full quarters.

The Ravens have usually struggled without Jackson. With Jackson as its starting quarterback, Baltimore is 82-38 (.683), including playoffs, and averages 27.6 points per game. Without Jackson as their starter since 2019, the Ravens are 7-15 (.318), including the postseason, and average 17.3 points per game.

text:
Joey Porter Jr. made it clear this week that his recent absences are due to injury, not contract issues.

"I don't even know where that narrative come from," the Dallas cornerback said Thursday, via ESPN. "I get it. It's the internet, but I really don't pay no attention to that or really care for that. My goal is to win games and play football, and that's what I want to do. So if there's any chance I could get on the field, I'm going to get on the field and do what I do best."

Porter joined the Cowboys following a trade from Pittsburgh ahead of Week 4 against Houston, when he first suffered a nagging ankle injury. He missed Week 5 against Tampa Bay due to a severe illness before returning for the next three games. He was inactive for last week’s win over the Colts due to the ankle/foot issue.

The 26-year-old sat out in Pittsburgh early this season due to a contract standoff, with reported back pain. That situation is coloring the current one with the Cowboys. However, Porter insists the two scenarios are completely different, noting his “whole foot is jacked up.”

"Just to be able to run, be able to cut," Porter said. "I play a position where I got to guard the most athletic people on the field, so if I can't run, skip or jump, then I'm no use out there."

The corner has not practiced this week. The question is whether he can do enough Friday to be ready for Sunday’s bout against the San Francisco 49ers.

"It's definitely frustrating. I'm on a new team and I want to show these guys what I can do, and I feel like I have been for the most part when I'm on the field," Porter said. "It's frustrating for everybody. I'm just trying to keep the main thing the main thing and get back as fast as possible to play with the guys."

The New York Giants' loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night helped the Cowboys' playoff chances considerably. Dallas now sits 1.5 games back in the NFC East race.

title: Puka Nacua Injury Update, Latest News on Rams WR's Status and Return Timeline Amid Knee Issue
description:

What's more, head coach Sean McVay said his expectation is Nacua will miss "extended time."

text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the foreseeable future.

The NFC West team placed the playmaker on injured reserve because of his MCL injury. What's more, head coach Sean McVay said his expectation is Nacua will miss "extended time."

This is a change in direction for the Rams, as McVay initially told reporters that even though the wide receiver was going to miss "a significant period of time," the plan was not to place him on IR due to "semantics with the roster."

Losing Nacua is quite the blow for Los Angeles seeing how Davante Adams is already sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Nacua's injury happened during Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders, although he still finished with a head-turning 14 receptions for 150 yards and one touchdown on 19 targets. Through seven games this season, he has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.

With both of Matthew Stafford's top receivers sidelined, the Rams will likely rely on the combination of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at the position. Tight end Tyler Higbee will likely see plenty of targets as well, although even he missed practice Thursday because of an illness.

Ultimately, the Rams are not going to be nearly as dangerous with both Nacua and Adams out.

Nacua is one of the best wide receivers in the league and someone Stafford routinely targets double-digit amounts of time per game. There will be more pressure on the rushing attack to carry the offense with the two top playmakers sidelined, and there is also little room for error in the NFC standings.

After all, Los Angeles is three games behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West at 5-4 and on the outside of the playoff picture looking in at this point. The Green Bay Packers have the final wild-card spot at 6-3 and will face the Rams in Week 12 while Nacua is still out.

With remaining games against the Packers, 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs, as well as two against the Seattle Seahawks, there is a real chance the Rams will miss the playoffs.

title: Why 49ers didn't add to D-line at trade deadline, per John Lynch - NBC Sports Bay Area
description:
Lynch noted Buckner, Osa Odhigizuwa, Nick Bosa, rookie Romello Height, Keion White, Mykel Williams and CJ West as key players on the defensive line.
San Francisco has not recorded a sack in their last two games.
"I think a lot of people might have some concern the last couple weeks; not a ton of sacks," Lynch admitted.
San Francisco 49ers Find the latest San Francisco 49ers news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Bay Area and California.
The defensive line wreaked havoc on the Raiders' rushing attack and allowed just 24 rushing yards, a season-best for the 49ers.
text:
Despite a season-ending injury to promising rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton, general manager John Lynch and the 49ers decided not to bolster their defensive front at Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.

With the addition of DeForest Buckner one week before, Lynch explained in an interview with KNBR's "Murph and Markus" Thursday that he's confident with San Francisco's defensive line as it is currently constructed and opted not to make any deals to add to the position group.

"If you've seen our history, I think that's always a spot -- you can't have enough good D-linemen," Lynch told Brian Murphy and Markus Boucher. "Now you do have a 53-man roster, too, and so, there's only so much you can do. But, we did make some calls. We inquired, but we really like our group."

Lynch noted Buckner, Osa Odhigizuwa, Nick Bosa, rookie Romello Height, Keion White, Mykel Williams and CJ West as key players on the defensive line. The 49ers have focused on bolstering the group through the draft, free agency and trade acquisition, and the team feels content with that depth allowing them all to rotate in and out to keep them fresh.

But, the 49ers have not been able to record many sacks this season. Their total of 15 sacks are the fifth-fewest in the NFL this season. San Francisco has not recorded a sack in their last two games.

Lynch notes that sacks are not the end-all, be-all metric for measuring defensive-line success.

"I think a lot of people might have some concern the last couple weeks; not a ton of sacks," Lynch admitted. "I would tell you that the game plans in those games, [then-Las Vegas Raiders quarterback] Kirk [Cousins] was getting rid of the ball really quick. We had like nine tackles for losses in that game. So, our group was doing some damage.

San Francisco 49ers

"And then when he held the ball, we were in his face. And so, I like where our pass rush is at. I think we'll finish at the quarterback the rest of the season, and I think we have ample assets in that group to go race them."

The defensive line wreaked havoc on the Raiders' rushing attack and allowed just 24 rushing yards, a season-best for the 49ers. They also recorded a season-high nine tackles for loss, as Lynch mentioned.

Lynch also believes that the defensive front's efficiency showed up in forcing three interceptions. And just because the sack total is low so far, it does not necessarily mean that trend will continue.

"You want to bring the quarterback down, but pressures are key ... they lead to turnovers," Lynch explained. "I would tell you that we were kind of at the bottom in turnovers and we had five and we've worked our way up. So, it can change really quickly.

"I've got a lot of belief in this defensive front and their ability to play at a high level and create chaos and things of that nature. I think we really believe in this group, so we think that will come."

The 49ers' defensive line will have their next challenge in Week 10 against the Dallas Cowboys, who have allowed just 14 sacks this season, the eighth-fewest in the NFL.

text:
LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Rams are placing star wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve after all. They announced the move on Thursday. Nacua must now miss at least the next four games.

The team signed wide receiver Brennan Presley from the practice squad to fill the roster spot. It also signed wide receiver Tyler Scott to the practice squad.

The move comes four days after Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and suffered turf toe on his 16th and final touch in a 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders. Coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Nacua would miss significant time, but that he would not go on IR due to “roster semantics.”

Teams can bring back eight players from IR during the season, and it’s becoming likely that Nacua will be the Rams’ seventh, leaving just one more.

The Rams have already used three of them on defensive end Myles Garrett, rookie tackle Keagen Trost and running back Ronnie Rivers. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is expected to be the fourth once he recovers from the hamstring injury he suffered last week, which should keep him out for a couple more weeks.

The Rams have until Nov. 25 to activate Ferguson if they want him to return this season.

Defensive end Kobie Turner and wide receiver Davante Adams are expected to be the fifth and sixth returns. If Nacua follows them, that would leave the Rams with just one spot left to return a player in the regular season. Teams do gain two additional return spots if they make the postseason.

Without Nacua or Adams on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, the Rams will look to a wide receiver room of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Presley.

After facing Arizona, the Rams will enter their bye before games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers, all of which Nacua will miss.

The Rams opted not to add a wide receiver at Tuesday’s trade deadline, believing Adams and Ferguson would return soon to bolster the passing game and that Nacua could return later this season.

"I think it is getting real close," Shanahan told Adam Copeland and Derek Papa. "But we look at it at the beginning of the week, every week, and see where he’s at, and he was a lot closer this week than last week, and hopefully, that continues next week.”

Evans has not practiced since he exited the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Washington Commanders in the second quarter due to his Achilles injury.

And even though Evans' competitive nature would allow him to play in a do-or-die situation, that's not the situation the 49ers find themselves in -- currently atop the NFC standings with a 7-1 record. Shanahan says the 49ers want him to return in a state where he is not at a risk of aggravation and forced to miss time after the fact.

"Mike’s such a dog and wants to get out there all the time, and I think it’d be hard to keep him out if this was the last game or anything like that," Shanahan explained. "But what we’re trying not to do is have him come back and then be out right away. We’re trying to build him up the right way, so hopefully, it can last a little bit.
